mainTopic: Whether burning the קומץ with a wrong intent about the לבונה creates פגול; the end of פרק הקומץ את המנחה; and the new משנה on mismatched intents, with רבי אליעזר's source
overview: This amud deals with a מנחה, whose קומץ and לבונה together act as the מתיר that permits the rest of the offering. The חריפי דפומבדיתא say that burning the קומץ with a plan to burn the לבונה too late makes the מנחה פגול, even according to the רבנן. רבא tries to prove this from a משנה, but the גמרא rejects the proof. רב חסדא, in the name of רב, rules the opposite: the קומץ does not permit the לבונה, so an intent about the לבונה cannot create פגול. A proof for רב from the case of two lambs is pushed aside, because the קומץ and לבונה share one vessel. רבי חנינא rules that a chain of wrong intents covering the whole מנחה makes it פגול, and רב אדא בר אהבה explains why his case had to be worded that way. A ברייתא saying 'everyone agrees it is פגול' is corrected to read 'everyone agrees it is פסול'. The פרק then ends, and a new משנה begins about intents to eat what is normally burned or burn what is normally eaten. The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's source in the doubled 'האכל יאכל', and asks how the רבנן use that wording; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The sharp ones of Pumbedita: burning can create פגול through burning
steps.stepSummary: The חריפי דפומבדיתא rule that burning the קומץ with intent to burn the לבונה at the wrong time makes the מנחה פגול. This works even according to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sharp scholars of Pumbedita say: burning can make an offering פגול through an intent about burning. This is true even according to the רבנן, who say you cannot create פגול with only half of the מתיר. Their rule applies only when, during the קומץ, he intended about the leftovers and had no intent about the לבונה. But here he intended about the לבונה, so it is as if he intended about the entire מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The חריפי דפומבדיתא state a new rule. Burning the קומץ while planning to burn the לבונה the next day makes the מנחה פגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן normally say that a פגול intent during only half of the מתיר (just the קומץ) does nothing. The חריפי דפומבדיתא explain that this rule applies only when the intent was about the שירים and the לבונה was left out of the thought. When the thought itself is about the לבונה, it reaches both halves of the מתיר, so it counts as covering the whole מתיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The sharp-minded scholars of the city of Pumbedita
Burning a part of the offering on the מזבח
Makes the offering פגול through a wrong-time intent
Half of the permitting factor, for example the קומץ without the לבונה
The leftover part of the מנחה, which the כהנים eat
Frankincense, which is burned together with the קומץ

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'burnings' here. The first הקטרה is the act being done right now: burning the קומץ. The second הקטרה is the plan in his mind: burning the לבונה tomorrow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that the רבנן's 'half מתיר' rule depends on what the thought was about, not only on which object was being offered at that moment.

phrases.english: The sharp ones of Pumbedita [say]:
Burning renders piggul [through intent about] burning,
phrases.notes: He burns the קומץ now while planning to burn the לבונה too late.

phrases.english: and even according to the Rabbis, who say
one does not render piggul with half a permitting factor —
these words apply only where
he had intent during it about the remainder
and the frankincense stands as it is,
phrases.notes: Meaning he had no thought at all about the לבונה.

phrases.english: but here, where he had intent about the frankincense —

phrases.aramaic: כְּמָה דְּחַשֵּׁב בֵּיהּ בְּכוּלֵּיהּ מַתִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: it is as though he had intent regarding the entire permitting factor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of פגול in a מנחה, with the opening words of this statement coming just before this line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning the קומץ with intent to burn the לבונה beyond its time creates פגול, even according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רבא quotes a משנה listing all four services
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the general rule of the משנה about פגול intents during the four services of a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: we also learned this in a משנה. This is the rule: anyone who takes the קומץ, puts it in a vessel, carries it, or burns it, while intending to eat what is normally eaten or to burn what is normally burned, outside its place, the offering is unfit but there is no כרת. If he intended outside its time, it is פגול and there is כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says he can support the חריפי דפומבדיתא from a משנה, and he quotes it. This step lays out the source; the actual inference comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists four services, and burning is one of them. It also lists two kinds of intent: eating and burning. The משנה does not say that burning follows different rules from the other three services.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this in a משנה, a phrase that introduces a supporting source
This is the general rule
Takes the handful of flour out of the מנחה
Outside its proper place, which makes the offering פסול without כרת
Beyond its proper time, which makes the offering פגול
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פגול

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: We too have learned it in a mishna:
This is the principle:
anyone who removes the handful, or places it in a vessel,
or who carries it, or who burns it,
intending to eat an item that is normally eaten
or to burn an item that is normally burned,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ – פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: outside its place — it is unfit, but there is no karet;

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ – פִּגּוּל וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: beyond its time — it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support the ruling of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling of the חריפי דפומבדיתא that burning creates פגול through intent about burning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 12a, which gives one general rule for all four services and both kinds of intent.

steps.title: רבא's inference: burning works like the other services
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that burning should follow the same pattern as the other three services, so intent about burning would count during burning too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't burning just like the others? Just as for the others, an intent either to eat or to burn creates פגול, so too for burning, an intent either to eat or to burn creates פגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now draws the proof out of the משנה he quoted. Since burning is listed together with the other services, it should follow the same rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first three services, an intent to burn the לבונה tomorrow clearly creates פגול. If burning is treated exactly like them, then burning the קומץ with intent to burn the לבונה tomorrow also creates פגול. That is exactly the ruling of the חריפי דפומבדיתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not that...? A phrase that introduces a proposed inference
Similar to; following the same pattern
Those, meaning the other three services

phrases.english: What, is it not that burning is similar to those?
phrases.notes: 'Those' means taking the קומץ, putting it in a vessel, and carrying it.

phrases.aramaic: מָה הָנָךְ – בֵּין לֶאֱכוֹל בֵּין לְהַקְטִיר,
phrases.english: Just as with those — whether to eat or to burn,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַקְטָרָה – בֵּין לֶאֱכוֹל בֵּין לְהַקְטִיר?
phrases.english: so too with burning — whether to eat or to burn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof out of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: Burning the קומץ with intent to burn the לבונה beyond its time creates פגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the משנה lists burning together with the other services under one rule.

steps.title: Rejection: burning may be different from the other services
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Burning might work only with an intent to eat, not with an intent to burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. For the other services, either an intent to eat or an intent to burn creates פגול. For burning, an intent to eat does, but an intent to burn does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. The משנה can be read in a way that does not support the חריפי דפומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list does not force us to treat all four services the same in every detail. It is possible that during burning, only an intent to eat the שירים late creates פגול, while an intent to burn the לבונה late does not. Since that reading is possible, the משנה is no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: No, a word that rejects the proposed proof
Yes

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof from the משנה is rejected, because burning may count as פגול only with an intent to eat. The ruling of the חריפי דפומבדיתא still stands, but it has no proof from this משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: A דחיה does not prove the חריפי דפומבדיתא wrong. It only shows that this משנה cannot prove them right.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, הָנָךְ – בֵּין לֶאֱכוֹל בֵּין לְהַקְטִיר;
phrases.english: No: with those — whether to eat or to burn;
with burning — to eat, yes; to burn, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, הָנָךְ – בֵּין לֶאֱכוֹל בֵּין לְהַקְטִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not the ruling of the חריפי דפומבדיתא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes burning follows every detail of the other services. The משנה can instead be read so that, during burning, only an intent to eat creates פגול.

steps.title: Burning does not make burning פגול, even for רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר גדא says in the name of רב חסדא that burning the קומץ with an intent about burning the לבונה at the wrong time does not make the מנחה פגול. This is true even according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר גדא sat before אביי and said in the name of רב חסדא: burning cannot make burning פגול. This is true even according to רבי מאיר, who says you can make an offering פגול with intent during only half of the things that permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion is brought that disagrees with the חריפי דפומבדיתא from Step 1. It says that a wrong intent about burning, made while burning, does not create פגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חריפי דפומבדיתא said that burning the קומץ while intending to burn the לבונה tomorrow makes the מנחה פגול. רב חסדא says it does not. He adds that even רבי מאיר, who is usually the easier one on making פגול (he allows it with half a מתיר), would agree here.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning a part of the offering on the מזבח
Makes the offering פגול (disqualified because of a wrong-time intent)
Half of the permitting factor, for example just the קומץ without the לבונה
An offering ruined by an intent to eat or burn it after its proper time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of intent. The question here is an intent to BURN at the wrong time. An intent to EAT the leftovers at the wrong time is a different case.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר גַּדָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Gadda sat before Abaye,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב וְקָא אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: and as he sat he said in the name of Rav Ḥisda:
Burning does not make burning piggul,
and even according to Rabbi Meir,
who says: 'One can make piggul during half of a permitting factor' –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that goes against the חריפי דפומבדיתא, after Step 4 showed that רבא's proof for them was not decisive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intent about burning the לבונה, made while burning the קומץ, does not make the מנחה פגול. This holds even for רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר agrees: the קומץ does not permit the לבונה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's rule about half a מתיר applies only to an intent about the leftovers, which the קומץ permits. The קומץ does not permit the לבונה, so it cannot make the offering פגול through the לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר's rule only applies when the person had a wrong intent about the leftovers, since the קומץ is what permits them. But here the קומץ is not what permits the לבונה, so it cannot make the offering פגול through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker explains why even רבי מאיר would agree. He answers the obvious question: doesn't רבי מאיר allow פגול with half a מתיר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: פגול only works when the service being done is the thing that permits the item you have bad intent about. The קומץ permits the שיריים to be eaten. The לבונה, however, is burned on its own merits and is not 'permitted' by the קומץ. So an intent about the לבונה, made during the קומץ, has nothing to grab onto.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover flour of the מנחה, eaten by the כהנים
The handful of flour taken from the מנחה and burned
Frankincense, burned together with the קומץ
The permitting factor, the service that makes something else allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key principle: you can only create פגול through a service that is the מתיר of the item your intent is about.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּחַשֵּׁב בְּהוּ בְּשִׁירַיִם,
phrases.english: That applies only where he had intent about the leftovers,
since the handful is their permitting factor,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּקוֹמֶץ לָאו מַתִּיר דִּלְבוֹנָה הוּא –
phrases.english: but here, where the handful is not the permitting factor of the frankincense –
he cannot make it piggul through it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּחַשֵּׁב בְּהוּ בְּשִׁירַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same statement of רב מנשיא בר גדא in the name of רב חסדא, explaining the 'even according to רבי מאיר' part of Step 5. No challenge was raised; this is the speaker's own reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the rule about half a מתיר works only where the service actually permits the item the intent is about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי מאיר, who allows פגול with half a מתיר, would also allow it here.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קומץ permits the שיריים, not the לבונה, so here even רבי מאיר agrees there is no פגול.

steps.title: אביי asks whether this came from רב
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב מנשיא whether רב חסדא said this rule in the name of his teacher רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Tell me, my master, did רב חסדא say this in the name of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי wants to know where the ruling originally came from. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing about the law changes here. אביי is checking whether this is only רב חסדא's own idea or a tradition from רב, which would give it more weight.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Answer me, my master', a polite way of asking a question

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Answer me, my master: is it in the name of Rav?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether רב חסדא received this rule from his teacher רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the source of the ruling in Steps 5–6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב חסדא's ruling came from רב.

steps.title: Yes, it is from רב, and it is also recorded that way
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא says yes. The גמרא adds that it was also recorded elsewhere that רב חסדא said in the name of רב: burning does not make burning פגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. It was also stated: רב חסדא said in the name of רב: burning does not make burning פגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered: the rule comes from רב. The גמרא backs this up with a separate report that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ruling stands as the opinion of רב himself, not only רב חסדא. The extra report confirms that the chain of tradition is reliable.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
It was also stated:
Rav Ḥisda said that Rav said:
Burning does not make burning piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the ruling is from רב, and a separate report confirms it.

steps.title: Support from the case of the two lambs
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אידי, in the name of אביי, brings a משנה about two lambs. A wrong intent about one lamb's own meat makes it פגול. A wrong intent about the other lamb's meat leaves both kosher. He suggests the reason is that one lamb is not the מתיר of the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב בר אידי said in the name of אביי: We also learned this in a משנה. If someone slaughtered one of the lambs intending to eat from it tomorrow, that lamb is פגול and the other one is kosher. If he intended to eat from the other lamb tomorrow, both are kosher. Why? Isn't it because the first lamb is not what permits the second, so it cannot make it פגול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from a משנה for רב's rule. The service of one item cannot make a different item פגול if it does not permit that item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering lamb A permits lamb A, not lamb B. So a wrong intent about lamb B, made while slaughtering lamb A, does nothing. In the same way, the קומץ does not permit the לבונה, so a wrong intent about the לבונה during the קומץ does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs
Its fellow, the other one of the pair
Valid, kosher for the offering
What is the reason?

steps.whatToRemember: רב יעקב בר אידי suggests that the two-lambs משנה supports רב: one lamb is not the מתיר of the other, just as the קומץ is not the מתיר of the לבונה. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two-lambs case is offered as a model from a משנה for the principle 'no מתיר, no פגול,' which would challenge the חריפי דפומבדיתא. Step 10 then shows why the comparison may not hold.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov bar Idi said in the name of Abaye:
We too have learned this in a mishna:
If one slaughtered one of the lambs
phrases.notes: The משנה is about a pair of lambs brought together as one offering.

phrases.english: intending to eat from it tomorrow –
it is piggul and the other one is valid;
if he intended to eat from the other one tomorrow –
both are valid.
What is the reason?
Is it not because, since
it is not the permitting factor of the other,
it cannot make it piggul?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a משנה for רב's ruling, now confirmed in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that the burning of the קומץ cannot make the לבונה פגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the two lambs: a wrong intent about the other lamb leaves both kosher, because one lamb is not the other's מתיר.

steps.title: The two lambs are separate, but the קומץ and לבונה share one vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the two lambs. Two lambs were never joined, but the קומץ and the לבונה were placed in one vessel, so they count as one item.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The lambs are different, because they were never set together in one vessel. Here, the קומץ and the לבונה were set together in one vessel, so they are treated like one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the two lambs in step 9. It says that case cannot teach us about the קומץ and the לבונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the lamb case, each animal stands on its own, so a wrong intent about one cannot affect the other. The קומץ and the לבונה, however, were joined together in one vessel. Because of that, they may count as a single unit, and a wrong intent about one could make the other פגול.

keyTerms.meaning: was fixed or set (into a vessel)
in one vessel
they are like one item
there (the other case) / here (our case)

phrases.english: No; it is there
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה about the two lambs from the previous step.

phrases.english: that it was not fixed in one vessel,
but here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the קומץ and the לבונה of the מנחה.

phrases.english: where they were fixed in one vessel,
they are considered like one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, הָתָם הוּא דְּלָא אִיקְּבַע בְּחַד מָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects comparing the two lambs to the קומץ and לבונה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two lambs were never joined in one vessel. The קומץ and לבונה were, so they may count as one unit.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's ruling on a chain of wrong intents
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא treasures a ruling from רבי חנינא. If one burns the קומץ intending to burn the לבונה the next day, and then burns the לבונה intending to eat the שירים the next day, the מנחה is פגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: רבי חנינא taught me this, and to me it is worth as much as all my learning. If someone burned the קומץ with the intent to burn the לבונה tomorrow, and burned the לבונה with the intent to eat the leftovers tomorrow, the offering is פגול.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching is brought. רב המנונא quotes a ruling from his teacher רבי חנינא about a wrong intent passed along from step to step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two wrong intents here. The first comes while burning the קומץ, about the לבונה. The second comes while burning the לבונה, about the leftovers. The ruling is that together they make the מנחה פגול, and the גמרא will next ask what exactly this teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: he made me absorb it; he taught it to me deeply
an offering made unfit by an intent to do a service at the wrong time
the handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the altar
frankincense, also burned on the altar
the leftover part of the מנחה, eaten by the כהנים

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא אַבְלַע לִי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina helped me absorb this matter,
and to me it weighs as much as all my learning:
if one burned the handful with intent to burn the frankincense,
phrases.notes: It is assumed that the plan is to burn it the next day, which is the wrong time.

phrases.english: and the frankincense with intent to eat the remainder tomorrow,
it is piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: הָא מִילְּתָא אַבְלַע לִי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, related ruling about פגול intent passing from the קומץ to the לבונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wrong intent during the burning of the קומץ about the לבונה, plus a wrong intent during the burning of the לבונה about the שירים, makes the מנחה פגול.

steps.title: What does רבי חנינא's ruling add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the ruling seems poorly worded. Whatever new idea it means to teach, it could have taught that idea in a simpler case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? If he means that burning can make burning פגול, he should have said only 'burned the קומץ to burn the לבונה.' If he means that half a מתיר can make the offering פגול, he should have said 'burned the קומץ to eat the leftovers tomorrow.' If he means both, he should have said 'burned the קומץ to burn the לבונה and to eat the leftovers tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא's case. It tests every possible lesson and shows that each one could have been stated more simply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case seems to involve two new ideas: that burning makes burning פגול, and that half a מתיר can cause פגול. For each idea, or for both together, there is a simpler case that would teach it. So the chain of two separate burnings with two intents seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: what new thing is he teaching us?
one burning can make another burning פגול
half of the items that permit the offering (only the קומץ, without the לבונה)
both of them

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

phrases.aramaic: אִי הַקְטָרָה מְפַגֶּלֶת הַקְטָרָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן –
phrases.english: If he is teaching us that burning renders burning piggul,
let him say: "He burned the handful to burn the frankincense"!

phrases.aramaic: אִי מְפַגְּלִין בַּחֲצִי מַתִּיר קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן –
phrases.english: If he is teaching us that one renders piggul with half a permitting factor,
phrases.notes: The קומץ and the לבונה together permit the שירים, so burning just one of them is "half" of what permits them.

phrases.english: let him say: "He burned the handful to eat the remainder tomorrow"!

phrases.aramaic: אִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ אֲתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן –
phrases.english: If he comes to teach us both,
let him say: "He burned the handful to burn the frankincense
and to eat the remainder tomorrow"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? אִי הַקְטָרָה מְפַגֶּלֶת הַקְטָרָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording and the purpose of רבי חנינא's ruling in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבי חנינא worded his case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each possible lesson, or both lessons together, could be taught by a simpler case. So the two-step case seems unneeded.

steps.title: The wrong intent covered the entire מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that רבי חנינא holds neither rule on its own. The מנחה is פגול only because the wrong intent spread across the whole מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: Really, he holds that burning does not make burning פגול, and that half a מתיר cannot make the offering פגול. This case is different, because the wrong intent spread over the entire מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the challenge. He says the ruling teaches a third idea, not either of the two ideas the גמרא suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each simpler case would not be פגול in רבי חנינא's view. Only here does the wrong intent touch every part of the מנחה: the קומץ, the לבונה and the שירים. That full coverage is what makes it פגול, so the longer case was necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: really; in truth (used to reject the earlier guesses)
here it is different
the intent spread out
meal offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אדא בר אהבה, רבי חנינא holds that burning does not make burning פגול, and that half a מתיר cannot cause פגול. A מנחה becomes פגול here only because the wrong intent spread over the entire offering.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי חנינא as agreeing with either of the two rules. He rejects both. The פגול comes only from the combined intent covering everything.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Actually, he holds
that burning does not render burning piggul,
and one does not render piggul with half a permitting factor,
but here is different,
since the intent spread over the entire meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a third reason that neither of the two suggested rules explains.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the ruling had to teach that burning makes burning פגול, or that half a מתיר causes פגול, or both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither rule is accepted. The מנחה is פגול only because the wrong intent covered the entire offering, which is why the longer case was needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a wrong intent which reaches every part of the מנחה can make it פגול, even though the separate parts of that intent would not do so on their own.

steps.title: A ברייתא says everyone agrees the מנחה is פגול
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב יצחק בר אבא. It says that if one burns the קומץ intending to eat the שירים at the wrong time, everyone agrees the מנחה is פגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reciter taught before רב יצחק בר אבא: If someone burned the handful intending to eat the leftovers the next day, everyone agrees it is פגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא about burning the קומץ with a wrong intent about the שירים. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'לדברי הכל,' meaning no one disagrees. That claim is the problem, because the earlier משנה records an argument on this very case.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a reciter whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
The leftover part of the מנחה, eaten by the כהנים
According to everyone; no one disagrees
An offering ruined by intent to eat or burn it after its proper time; eating it carries כרת

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: A reciter taught before Rav Yitzchak bar Abba:
If one burned the handful intending to eat the leftovers –
phrases.notes: The ברייתא means eating them the next day, which is past their allowed time.

phrases.english: everyone agrees it is piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא about the same topic of wrong intent during burning the קומץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning the קומץ with intent to eat the שירים the next day makes the מנחה פגול according to everyone.

steps.title: But רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree on this case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. How can it say 'everyone agrees' when the משנה records an argument on this exact case?
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't they argue about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the words 'everyone agrees' don't fit. The earlier משנה shows that רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says this case is פגול. The חכמים say it is not פגול unless the wrong intent covers the whole מתיר. So the ברייתא cannot say everyone agrees it is פגול.

keyTerms.meaning: They truly argue

phrases.english: But don't they argue about it?
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי מאיר and the חכמים in the משנה earlier in this פרק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'לדברי הכל פגול' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה records a מחלוקת on this case, so 'everyone agrees' cannot be correct.

steps.title: Fix the wording: everyone agrees it is פסול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the ברייתא to read 'everyone agrees it is פסול.' Even the חכמים agree the מנחה is disqualified, though not פגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: everyone agrees it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by correcting one word in the ברייתא, from 'פגול' to 'פסול.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and the חכמים only argue about whether it is פגול, which carries כרת. Both sides agree the offering is ruined (פסול). With the change, 'everyone agrees' is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא changes the wording of a source
Disqualified (invalid). "Everyone agrees it is פסול" means both sides agree the מנחה is invalid; it does not say there is no כרת, since רבי מאיר still holds it is פגול, with כרת.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
everyone agrees it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by fixing the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says everyone agrees it is פגול, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really says everyone agrees it is פסול, which both רבי מאיר and the חכמים accept.
steps.confusionAlert: פגול and פסול are not the same word. פגול is a kind of invalid offering that carries כרת; פסול simply means disqualified. "Everyone agrees it is פסול" only says everyone agrees it is invalid. It does not say that no one holds it carries כרת: רבי מאיר still calls it פגול, with כרת, and the חכמים agree only that it is invalid.

steps.title: Why not fix it to say 'it is פגול, following רבי מאיר'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it chose this correction. It could have changed the ברייתא to 'it is פגול,' and said the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it say: 'it is פגול,' and this ברייתא follows רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own fix. It offers a different correction that seems just as good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we are already changing words, we could keep 'פגול' and change 'everyone agrees' to 'this is so,' which matches רבי מאיר. Why change the ruling itself instead of who holds it?

keyTerms.meaning: But let it say: offering a different reading
This is (so): a plain ruling, not claiming everyone agrees

phrases.english: But let it say: 'this is piggul,'
and it follows Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא: הֲרֵי זֶה פִּגּוּל, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the correction given in the previous step.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another correction keeps the ruling of פגול and simply assigns the ברייתא to רבי מאיר. Why not choose that one?

steps.title: A reciter mixes up one word, not a whole phrase
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the reciter was surely taught 'everyone agrees.' He could easily swap the word פגול for פסול, but not mix up 'הרי זה' with 'דברי הכל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The reciter was taught 'everyone agrees.' He could mix up 'פגול' with 'פסול,' but he would not mix up 'this is' with 'everyone agrees.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its first correction. It shows that this correction fits the kind of mistake a reciter might really make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פגול and פסול sound alike, so a reciter could easily say one instead of the other. 'הרי זה' and 'דברי הכל' are completely different words, so that mix-up is unlikely. Our fix should match the likely mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught him: what the reciter was originally taught
He would get it mixed up

phrases.english: The reciter was taught 'everyone agrees,'
phrases.notes: Literally 'they taught the reciter.' The point is that 'everyone agrees' was surely in the original wording.

phrases.english: he could mix up 'piggul' with 'disqualified,'
but 'this is' with 'everyone agrees'
he would not mix up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 and confirms the correction of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing which reading is more likely
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the swap of פגול for פסול is a believable mistake, so the ברייתא should read 'everyone agrees it is פסול.'
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא really says: if one burns the קומץ intending to eat the שירים the next day, everyone agrees the מנחה is פסול. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue only about whether it is also פגול.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הקומץ את המנחה
steps.stepSummary: The פרק 'הקומץ את המנחה' ends here with the traditional הדרן line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק 'הקומץ את המנחה.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן is said at the end of every פרק. It marks that the topic of this פרק is finished and a new one is about to start.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing words said at the end of a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who removes a handful from the meal offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק 'הקומץ את המנחה' is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: intending to eat what isn't eaten, or burn what isn't burned
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה. If one takes the קומץ intending to eat, past its time, something not normally eaten, or to burn something not normally burned, the מנחה is כשר. רבי אליעזר disqualifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who takes the handful from a מנחה intending to eat something that is not normally eaten, or to burn something that is not normally burned, past its time: it is כשר. רבי אליעזר disqualifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins the next פרק. It asks what happens when the wrong intent is about the wrong kind of action: eating the part meant for burning, or burning the part meant for eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ is meant to be burned, not eaten. The שירים are meant to be eaten, not burned. The תנא קמא says a wrong-time intent that mixes these up does not ruin the מנחה. רבי אליעזר says it does make it פסול, though not פגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a משנה
Whose normal way is not: something not usually done with that item
Valid; the offering is fine
Disqualifies

steps.confusionAlert: Watch which part is which. 'Eating what is not normally eaten' means the קומץ. 'Burning what is not normally burned' means the שירים.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who removes a handful from the meal offering
intending to eat something that is not normally eaten,
phrases.notes: He means the קומץ, which goes on the מזבח. The intent is to eat it after its proper time.

phrases.english: or to burn something that is not normally burned –
phrases.notes: He means the שירים, which the כהנים normally eat.

phrases.english: it is valid; Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַקּוֹמֵץ אֶת הַמִּנְחָה לֶאֱכוֹל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wrong-time intent to eat what is normally burned, or burn what is normally eaten, leaves the מנחה כשר. רבי אליעזר holds it is פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next פרק's question: does a wrong intent count only when it matches the normal use of that part of the offering?

steps.title: The משנה's final cases: less than an olive and half plus half
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. An improper intention about less than a כזית does not disqualify the מנחה. Half a כזית of eating plus half a כזית of burning also does not disqualify it, because eating and burning do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he intends (with an improper intention, like past its time) to eat something that is normally eaten, or to burn something that is normally burned, but less than an olive's volume, the מנחה is fit. If he intends to eat half an olive's volume and burn half an olive's volume, it is fit, because eating and burning do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from the last step is finishing its list of cases. It adds two more cases where the מנחה stays fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An intention only disqualifies when it is about at least a כזית. So even a 'normal' intention (eating what people eat, burning what goes on the מזבח) does nothing if it is about less than a כזית. Also, half a כזית of eating and half a כזית of burning cannot be added together to reach a full כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than an olive's volume, the minimum amount for an intention to count
Half an olive's volume
Burning on the מזבח
Combine, join together to reach the needed amount
Fit, valid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'eating' and 'burning' are the same act here just because the גמרא will soon call burning 'eating'. In this משנה they cannot be added together to make one כזית.

phrases.english: To eat something that is normally eaten,
phrases.notes: He means with an improper intention, like eating it past its time, the same kind of intention as the earlier cases in the משנה.

phrases.english: and to burn something that is normally burned,
less than an olive's volume, it is fit.
To eat half an olive's volume
and to burn half an olive's volume, it is fit,
because eating and burning do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה begun in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention about less than a כזית does not disqualify, and half a כזית of eating plus half a כזית of burning do not combine.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. רבי אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן, asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's ruling that intending to eat or burn something not normally eaten or burned disqualifies the מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי says in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking where רבי אליעזר gets his ruling from. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an intention only counts if it fits how the item is used: eating what people eat, burning what is burned. רבי אליעזר disqualifies even a 'mismatched' intention, so the גמרא wants his source.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה
What is the reason, what is the source?

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Asi says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי אליעזר's view.

steps.title: Two kinds of eating in one verse
steps.stepSummary: The doubled word 'האכל יאכל' teaches two kinds of eating: by a person and by the מזבח. Just as a wrong intention works for a person's eating, it works for the מזבח's eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says, 'And if it is at all eaten from the meat of his peace-offering.' The double word means the verse is talking about two kinds of eating, one by a person and one by the מזבח. This teaches you that just as an intention about a person's eating counts, an intention about the מזבח's eating counts too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question with a פסוק. The double wording 'האכל יאכל' shows that the Torah has two kinds of eating in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about פיגול uses the word for eating twice. One 'eating' is people eating the קרבן, and the other is the fire of the מזבח 'eating' it. So an improper intention about the burning counts just like one about the eating.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is at all eaten': a doubled verb that is read as teaching something extra
Eating by a person, like the כהנים or the owner
The מזבח's 'eating', meaning the burning on the fire
Have an intention (מחשבה) that can disqualify a קרבן

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And if it is at all eaten
from the meat of his peace-offering"
the verse is speaking of two kinds of eating,
one is eating by a person
and one is eating by the altar,
to tell you:
just as an intention counts regarding a person's eating,
so too an intention counts regarding the altar's eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb teaches two kinds of eating, by a person and by the מזבח, so intention works for both.

steps.title: Crossing between the person and the altar
steps.stepSummary: The same verse also teaches a 'crossed' intention. Planning for people to eat what belongs on the מזבח, or for the מזבח to burn what belongs to people, also counts. This is exactly רבי אליעזר's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as an intention counts when people's food is planned for people, and the מזבח's portion is planned for the מזבח, so too it counts when people's food is planned for the מזבח, and the מזבח's portion is planned for people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן takes the lesson one step further. It now explains רבי אליעזר's actual ruling about mismatched intentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step only said intention works for each kind of eating separately. Now he adds that the two can be swapped: planning to burn the שיריים (meant for people) or to eat the קומץ (meant for the מזבח) past its time also disqualifies. That is what רבי אליעזר meant by 'something not normally eaten or burned.'

keyTerms.meaning: From people's portion to the מזבח: intending to burn what is meant to be eaten
From the מזבח's portion to people: intending to eat what is meant to be burned

steps.whyThisMatters: This crossed intention is the whole point of disagreement between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים in the משנה.

phrases.english: And just as one can have an intention
from what is eaten by a person to eating by a person,
phrases.notes: He means planning that a part meant for people will be eaten by people, but past its time.

phrases.english: and from what is eaten by the altar to eating by the altar,
so too one can have an intention from what is eaten by a person to the altar,
and from what is eaten by the altar to a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁמְּחַשְּׁבִין מֵאֲכִילַת אָדָם לַאֲכִילַת אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the lesson of step 23 to crossed intentions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Intention also counts when it crosses between people's portion and the מזבח's portion.

steps.title: Why can the two be crossed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we may cross between a person's eating and the מזבח's eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the verse lets us swap the two kinds of eating. This sets up a short answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the verse covers two kinds of eating does not yet explain why one can be swapped for the other. The גמרא wants the logic behind the crossing.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a person's eating and the מזבח's eating may be swapped.

steps.title: The Torah calls burning 'eating'
steps.stepSummary: Because the Torah describes burning on the מזבח with the word for eating, the two are treated as one category, so intentions can cross between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the Merciful One described burning using the language of eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah itself uses the word 'eating' for burning. That is why the two can be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah put burning under the word 'eating', burning is a kind of eating. So a plan to 'eat' the מזבח's portion or 'burn' people's portion is still an intention about eating, and it counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Expressed it, brought it out (in certain words)
The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the תורה
The language of eating

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה calls burning 'eating.' רבי אליעזר learns from this that a wrong intention can cross between people's portion and the מזבח's portion and still disqualify the מנחה.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One expressed burning
using the language of eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Burning is called eating in the תורה, so the two categories can be swapped.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from the eating language?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who reject רבי אליעזר's crossed intentions, explain the Torah's use of eating language for the מזבח's burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with the fact that the Torah described the burning in the language of eating?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question for the רבנן, and the answer comes at the start of the next amud. If they disagree with רבי אליעזר, what do they learn from the תורה calling burning 'eating'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר used the eating language to put people's eating and the מזבח's burning into one category, so a plan can cross from one to the other. The רבנן do not allow that crossing. So the גמרא assumes the Torah's wording must still teach them something else, and it asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, meaning the majority of sages who disagree with רבי אליעזר here
Literally 'the Merciful One.' The גמרא's usual way of saying 'the Torah' or 'ה׳ in the Torah.'
Literally 'brought them out.' Here it means 'expressed them' or 'worded them.'
The language of eating, meaning the Torah's use of the word 'eating'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the רבנן deny that the Torah calls burning 'eating.' Everyone agrees about the wording. They only disagree about what that wording teaches.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
this, that the Merciful One expressed them in the language of eating,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי דְּאַפְּקִינְהוּ רַחֲמָנָא בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 26 explained how רבי אליעזר uses the eating language for burning. This step turns to the opposing view and asks how the רבנן use that same wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson do the רבנן draw from the Torah describing the מזבח's burning with the word for eating, since they do not use it to allow crossed intentions?
